claims.text: "Fighting in Masisi has displaced more than 24,000 people since mid-September."

"...more than 3,000 people fled Rhoe displacement camp in Djugu territory (also in Ituri province) following clashes that intensified on 27 September. According to the UN aid coordination office, OCHA, at least four people were reportedly killed and seven injured, while several houses were burned down in Blukwa."

"The camp had provided shelter for some 19,000 people fleeing violence in the resource-rich east of the country, close to the border with Rwanda. In recent days, thousands of people fled Kigonze following reports that soldiers had entered the site searching for weapons and people suspected of belonging to non-State armed groups." A separate UN News report (29 September 2026) cites OCHA: the camp "hosts nearly 19,000 displaced people" who have faced "armed violence, threats and intimidation against civilians, arrests, forced displacement and the destruction of shelters" since security incidents began on 20 September.

The same UN News report (1 October 2026) states that "a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down" at Bunia's Kigonze displacement camp, which "now lies abandoned," setting back the regional Ebola response; UN official Julien Harneis said: "It's been a huge struggle to create Ebola transit centres [and] Ebola treatment centres; it's required money, bringing in staff and it's been a struggle all across the east. So, when we lose a centre, that means we lose capacity, we lose investment and we have to start again."

A UN News report (13 November 2026) states WHO condemned an attack in Cantine-Aloya, North Kivu, that killed 66 civilians including three health workers and saw three health facilities looted, and that a nurse was killed and another health worker badly injured two weeks earlier while responding to an Ebola alert in Tshopo province; WFP warned nearly 29 million people in the DRC face acute food insecurity, with UN-backed IPC assessments projecting 30.3 million people in crisis levels of acute food insecurity or worse (including 4.2 million at emergency levels) between January and June 2027, concentrated in the conflict-affected eastern provinces.

description: Armed-group fighting across North Kivu and Ituri provinces, DR Congo, has displaced tens of thousands since mid-September 2026 and is undermining the region's Ebola response. Fighting in Masisi territory, North Kivu, has displaced more than 24,000 people since mid-September, while clashes near Djugu in Ituri forced over 3,000 people to flee the Rhoe displacement camp on 27 September, killing at least four and injuring seven, with houses burned in Blukwa. A military search operation at Bunia's Kigonze camp, which sheltered roughly 19,000 displaced people, triggered further flight and the destruction of a key Ebola transit centre. WHO has since condemned a mid-November attack on Cantine-Aloya, North Kivu, that killed 66 civilians including three health workers and saw three health facilities looted, following the killing of a nurse responding to an Ebola alert in Tshopo province two weeks earlier, as WFP warns nearly 29 million people in the DRC face acute food insecurity.

impact.summary: More than 24,000 people have been displaced by fighting in Masisi, North Kivu, since mid-September, and over 3,000 fled Ituri's Rhoe camp on 27 September after clashes killed four and injured seven, with houses burned in Blukwa. A military search operation at Bunia's Kigonze camp (sheltering roughly 19,000 people) triggered further flight and destroyed a key Ebola transit centre. WHO says an attack on Cantine-Aloya, North Kivu, in mid-November killed 66 civilians including three health workers and saw three facilities looted, following the killing of a nurse responding to an Ebola alert in Tshopo province two weeks earlier. WFP warns nearly 29 million people in the DRC face acute food insecurity, projected to reach 30.3 million in crisis levels (4.2 million at emergency level) by mid-2027.

location.region: Masisi territory (North Kivu) and Djugu territory / Bunia (Ituri)

event.scale: Armed-group clashes (CODECO vs. Convention for the Popular Revolution, and North Kivu fighting) driving mass displacement across two provinces

name: Conflict Displacement Surge — North Kivu & Ituri, DR Congo

updates.text: WHO condemned an attack on Cantine-Aloya, North Kivu, that killed 66 civilians including three health workers and saw three facilities looted, following the killing of a nurse responding to an Ebola alert in Tshopo two weeks earlier; WFP warned nearly 29 million DRC residents face acute food insecurity, projected to reach 30.3 million by mid-2027 (UN News).

UN News reported on 1 October that a key Ebola transit centre at Bunia's Kigonze displacement camp -- already destabilized by a security incursion in late September -- burned down and now lies abandoned, further disrupting the regional Ebola response alongside continuing displacement from fighting in Masisi and Ituri.
Clashes near Djugu, Ituri intensified, forcing over 3,000 people to flee Rhoe displacement camp; OCHA reported at least four killed and seven injured, with houses burned in Blukwa.

Security incidents began at Bunia's Kigonze displacement camp (sheltering ~19,000 people) after soldiers entered searching for weapons and suspected armed-group members; OCHA reported armed violence, intimidation, arrests and shelter destruction, prompting thousands to flee.
